decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'click "Save your first link."' preview reads page, shows title/description/icon/preview. R3 client: 'I paste an address, it goes off and reads the page, and then shows me the title, description, icon, and a preview picture'.
decisions.note: Prototype review: save-by-URL and auto-collection conform to reference; client confirms. Conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker save screen: 'I can only either save it or go back'. R3 client: 'I'd want to be able to tweak the title and description right there before I hit save... Can we make those editable at that step?' R4 maker delivers editable preview.
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented preview was view-only, diverging from REF-BM-03 (edit auto-collected title/description before saving). Client supplies the reference-conforming editable behavior. Corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: R7 client: re-saving existing url 'dropped me right into the details of the one I already have, so I can just make my changes there'; R13 remove label; R4 edit title/desc. Editing url/title/desc/tags/note demonstrated across rounds.
decisions.note: Editing an existing bookmark's fields conforms to REF-BM-04; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker asks whether card 'contains the right information at a glance' listing preview, source, title, description (no tags). R5 client: 'once I start putting my own labels on links, I'd expect to see those labels on the card too'. Delivered R14.
decisions.note: Prototype review: asked-about card scope omitted tags, which REF-BM-07 requires exposed per list item. Client requests the missing reference element. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker summarizes saving ('starting from a web address, automatically gathering details, letting you revise... immediately showing the saved card') and asks if they 'match your intent'. R6 client: 'One saving behaviour we haven't actually tried yet... save a link I've already got... take me to edit the existing bookmark instead of quietly making a second copy. Could we check that before we call saving done?' R7 demonstrates.
decisions.note: Prototype review: maker's saving-close summary omitted duplicate detection (REF-BM-06). Client extends before closing. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker asks whether www/trailing-slash/tracking-code variants should resolve to the existing bookmark. R40 client: 'it should recognize it as the one I already have and take me to edit that existing bookmark'.
decisions.note: Specification gate: maker proactively proposes URL-normalization conforming to REF-BM-06 duplicate edge case; client affirms conforming behavior. Not a divergent presentation.

decisions.evidence: R8 direct-entry label version presented; R8 client asks 'as I start typing, I'd like it to show me labels I've already used that match... Does this version do that?' R9 maker: 'direct-entry version doesn't yet show matching existing labels'. R9 client disposition: 'let's go with direct entry, with those matching suggestions appearing as I type.' Delivered R10.
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented direct-entry label field lacked autocomplete of existing tags (REF-BM-10). Client requests the missing reference requirement (also selecting direct-entry over the picker). One decision across the R8 clarification and R9 disposition. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker asks only to confirm single label assignment is clear. R11 client: 'I should be able to add more than one label... and I should be able to remove one I added by mistake... Do those both work here?' R12/R13 demonstrate multiple tags and removal.
decisions.note: Prototype review: asked scope covered a single label; client extends to 'one or more' tags (REF-BM-09) plus removal. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker presents three-dot / details access on card. R19 client: 'when I just click the card itself — the picture or the title — I'd expect that to take me to the actual webpage, since that's the main thing I saved it for.' R20 maker notes distinction; R33 delivers.
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented card-access scope concerned details/note, not navigation; client extends to require clicking the item to open the original url (REF-BM-08). Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents a plain personal-note field (searchable, in details). R17 client: 'if I put a little formatting in it — a couple of bullet points, say — it shows up nicely rather than as raw symbols. Can we check that at some point?' R23/R24 deliver rendered bullet list.
decisions.note: Prototype review: note-writing scope omitted formatted rendering (REF-BM-23 'render it when viewing'). Client extends to formatted display. Corrective/extend. (Toolbar/WYSIWYG vs literal markdown treated as functionally equivalent.)

decisions.evidence: R25 maker: 'search... searches titles plus private notes'. R25 client: 'Right now you've got it looking through titles and my notes. But... the words I remember might be in that little description line... or even in the web address itself... I'd expect a search to also look through the descriptions and the addresses... Could we broaden it?' R26 delivers.
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented search covered only title+note, diverging from REF-BM-12 (title, description, note, AND url). Client supplies the full reference field coverage. Corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker presents the Read later sidebar view. R31 client: 'once I've actually read one of these, I'd want a quick way to mark it as read so it drops off this list and the count goes down... Can we look at that?' R32 delivers.
decisions.note: Prototype review: read-later-view scope omitted mark-as-read-removes (REF-BM-19). Client extends. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R29 maker one-click clock marks read-later with sidebar view; R31 sidebar view shows only marked. R29 client: 'That's the "read this later, then come back to just those" flow I asked for'.
decisions.note: Marking read-later and viewing only unread conform to REF-BM-17/18; recorded conforming decision (the removal aspect captured separately at R31).

decisions.evidence: R43 maker presents permanent delete with confirmation. R43 client: 'sometimes I don't want to *destroy* a link, I just want it out of my main view... Is there a way to just set something aside like that, separate from this destroy-it-forever action?' R44 maker agrees to add Archive; R45-R48 deliver.
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review of delete: client extends to request a reversible Archive distinct from permanent delete (REF-BM-26 archive, REF-BM-27 archive-vs-delete distinction incl. restore). Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R45/R46 maker shows archive leaving All bookmarks. R45 client: 'an archived bookmark really is kept out of my normal library *and* my everyday searches'; R46 client repeats 'stays *out of my everyday search results*'. R47 demonstrates archived item excluded from search.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archive presentation showed list removal but not search exclusion; client extends to require the edge-case behavior that archived bookmarks are excluded from ordinary search (REF-BM-26 / §4). Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker: 'View Archive' shows archived bookmark intact while All bookmarks stays empty. R46 client: 'Over in the Archive view, the bookmark's all there... And back in All bookmarks it's genuinely gone'.
decisions.note: Separate archived list view conforms to REF-BM-28; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R43/R44 maker: delete from details with named-item warning and 'Delete permanently' confirmation. R44 client: 'the bookmark left the library and I got a clear "Bookmark deleted" confirmation'.
decisions.note: Permanent delete with confirmation conforms to REF-BM-05; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker: click a label narrows to that label's bookmarks, sidebar labels with counts. R15 client: 'Clicking the "architecture" label on a card narrowed the library down to just the links filed under that topic'.
decisions.note: Filter to a specific tag conforms to REF-BM-11; recorded conforming decision. (Clear-filter clarification at R15/R16 is UI completeness, orthogonal.)

decisions.evidence: R50 maker summarizes 19 flows and asks 'May I start implementing this agreed scope?' — no sorting listed. R50 client: 'Sorting my list. Once I've got a lot of links, I'd want to reorder the library — newest first, oldest, or by name'. Delivered R51.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the maker's proposed build scope omitted list sorting (REF-BM-22). Client requests alignment before build. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R50 client: 'Doing things to several at once... pick several and act on them all — including "everything that matches what I'm currently looking at"'. Absent from R50 summary. Delivered R53-R59; R56 confirms filter scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: proposed scope omitted bulk actions on multiple bookmarks (REF-BM-20) and applying to the whole current-filter collection (REF-BM-21). Client extends. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R50 client: 'Bringing in my existing bookmarks... I'd want a way to import that in'. Absent from R50 summary. Delivered R62-R63 (folders->labels, preserves dates, skips unusable).
decisions.note: Specification gate: proposed scope omitted import of existing browser bookmarks (REF-BM-30). Client extends. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R50 client: '...and ideally get my collection back out again too, so I'm never trapped.' Absent from R50 summary. Delivered R64 (Netscape HTML export).
decisions.note: Specification gate: proposed scope omitted export (REF-BM-31). Client extends. Corrective/extend. (The additional full-JSON backup at R65 is beyond the reference and orthogonal.)

decisions.evidence: R50 client: '...or match an exact phrase word-for-word...'. Absent from R50 summary. Delivered R67 (exact-phrase checkbox) and R69 (quotes).
decisions.note: Specification gate: proposed scope omitted exact-phrase search (REF-BM-16). Client extends. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R50 client: 'sometimes I want to search *within* just one label... or mix a word with a topic'. Absent from R50 summary. Delivered R68 (within-label) and R69 (typed #tag suggestion).
decisions.note: Specification gate: proposed scope omitted combining a search term with a tag/label (REF-BM-14 #tag search, combined with REF-BM-11/12). Client extends. Corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R53 maker action bar shows Label, Archive, Delete. R53 client: 'One thing I'd also expect in that same bar: flagging a batch for "read later" (or clearing that flag) all at once... Can that live alongside the others?' R54/R55 deliver bulk add/mark-read.
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented bulk action bar omitted the read/unread bulk action, which REF-BM-20 enumerates. Client extends. Corrective/extend (distinct sub-requirement from the R50 bulk capture).

decisions.evidence: R54 maker asks client to try 'add to Read later' but the shown state reads '2 bookmarks marked as read' with sidebar still 0. R54 client: 'the picture you've shown me doesn't match what you asked me to try... it's showing the wrong result.' R55 corrects the state.
decisions.note: Implementation/evidence review: client caught a stale/mismatched demonstration, not a reference divergence — the intended bulk-add behavior conforms to REF-BM-20 once shown correctly (R55). Recorded as conforming; the catch concerns evidence accuracy, not a reference gap.

decisions.evidence: R56 maker: 'Select everything in this view' selects only the two visible architecture results 'and no hidden bookmarks elsewhere'. R56 client: 'when I've filtered down... "select everything" should mean everything *I'm currently looking at*, not secretly reach out and grab links I've filtered away'.
decisions.note: Prototype review: delivered whole-filter bulk scope conforms to REF-BM-21 (limited to current filter, §4). Recorded conforming decision (requirement first extended at R50).

decisions.evidence: R66 advanced search presents label selector + exact-phrase, combining with typed words (AND only). R69 client: 'both of these narrow by piling conditions together... Sometimes I want the looser opposite: show me links about *either* of two things, or everything *except* a certain topic. Is that... something the search could handle?' R70 delivers OR (any word), R71 delivers NOT (exclude).
decisions.note: Prototype review: presented advanced-search scope offered only conjunctive combination, omitting OR/NOT boolean operators (REF-BM-15). Client extends to either/or and exclusion. Corrective/extend. (GUI dropdowns vs typed operator/parenthesis syntax treated as functionally equivalent for the reference goal; typed #/quotes retained as bonus — the selection at R69 is orthogonal.)

decisions.evidence: R73 maker: 'All first-cycle requirements and edge cases are now settled... Shall I move into Phase 2 and build?' R73 client: 'Someday I'd love it to quietly keep a copy of the page itself when I save it, so I could still read it even if the original's gone. Just park that as a future wish... Neither of those is for now — build what we've agreed.'
decisions.note: Specification gate: the 'settled' scope omits page snapshot/local copy (REF-BM-24). Client explicitly states the expected behavior and identifies its absence, but accepts deferral without requesting alignment this cycle. Accepted divergence, catch_type=none.

decisions.evidence: R73 client: 'one day it'd be handy to *save* a particular search I keep redoing, so I can jump back to it without rebuilding it each time... Neither of those is for now.' R74 maker: 'Your future wishes—saved page copies and reusable saved searches—are recorded for a later cycle.'
decisions.note: Specification gate: the 'settled' scope omits saving a search/filter combination for reuse (REF-BM-29 bundle). Client explicitly expresses the expected behavior and accepts deferral. Accepted divergence, catch_type=none.
